full_review:
First time trying nasi ayam gepuk at Gepuklah, and honestly, pretty impressed! 🍗🔥

First of all, the waiting time was CRAZY - around 1 hour 45 minutes. 😭 I know the place is popular and the queue can be long, but almost 2 hours is still quite a wait. Luckily, the weather wasn’t too hot that day, and thankfully the food made the wait somewhat worth it.

RM19.90 per set, and I think it’s quite reasonable considering the generous portion and free rice refill.

🍗 Chicken: My favourite part! The chicken is BIG, boneless, juicy and tender. The flavour surprisingly reminds me of KFC, but with a stronger black pepper twist. You can choose chopped or unchopped - both are good, but I personally enjoyed biting into the whole juicy piece. 😂

🌶️ Sambal: I ordered less spicy, expecting it to be super spicy based on what I heard before, but surprisingly it was very manageable for me. My friend had medium and also found it not very spicy. So spicy lovers, just level up!

🥜 Gajus sauce: THIS is the game changer. Super fragrant, rich and nutty from the cashew + peanut blend. A little jelak if eaten alone, but mix it with sambal + rice + chicken = 🔥.

🥣 And don’t forget the kicap manis / sweet dark soy sauce - honestly, on point! Sweet, savoury and so good when drizzled over the rice and chicken. Such a simple addition but it makes the whole thing even better.

🍚 Rice: Free refill is a big plus, although I was expecting more coconut fragrance since it’s called nasi lemak rice. Slightly disappointed there.

🥬 The vegetables were crunchy but way too little - basically gone in 3 bites. 😂 Would definitely appreciate a bigger portion.

🥤 Signature Ham Leng Chat: HUGE and super refreshing! Sprite + lemon + limau + sour plum. Honestly, one cup is enough for two people to share.

Overall, I can see why Gepuklah by Ming Chun is getting attention. The fried chicken version feels very approachable, especially with that black pepper flavour.

Would I come back? Yes.
Would I queue 1 hour 45 minutes again? …Let’s see. 😂

This was my first ayam gepuk experience, so my next mission is to try the more traditional ayam gepuk / ayam berempah style and see how it compares. 👀🍗

full_review:
Reached around 5.30pm and was lucky to only wait for about 20-30 minutes before it was my turn. i was really excited to try gepuklah bc the photos on social media looked so good and this was also one of my reasons for flying into kl.

I have to say I was also a bit disappointed. Maybe because I had high expectations but overall it wasn’t that wow. Starting from food presentation and portion, it’s really appetising and portion is really huge. However, food tasted cold (it was not really warm out of the kitchen). Sambal and bayam were good! Sambal had a good spicy kick and bayam was crispy just the way i like it. I like the rice (just nice for me because coconut rice can be quite filling for me) but some people may prefer it to be a bit more lemak to bring out the fragrance. Chicken really tasted like KFC chicken haha but wished it was warmer. Mushrooms were a bit oily. I felt while the flavours did complement together, the overall saltiness of the dish can be slightly reduced. Also got it with the Ham Leng Chat which was really a huge cup that I could only finish half of it. It’s a nice cleanser to the food but it tasted mostly like soda to me (calamansi taste not very pronounced).

Overall I think okay to try once if the queue isn’t long. Personally there are better ayam gepuks out there but still happy I came to try it for myself. Hopefully will have QC for the food to make sure taste is consistently in tip-top condition. ATB to mingchun and shoutout to the service team for being patient and giving a pleasant dining experience!
